title: Playlists
summary: A playlist is a pool of tracks that clocks take tracks from. It is not a queue: the order of tracks does not matter, and the system chooses which track plays. Its placement rule says how it is placed in clocks.

entities.text: A named set of tracks with a type, for example "Pop hits" of type music. Clocks are built from playlists.
The system picks a track from the playlist by its play rules and by the time left in the hour. You never set an order.

How the playlist is placed in every clock that uses it: Fill (fills the time left; the default), Spread N (N tracks spread over the hour), Start (the first track), End (the last track, ending at 60:00), Start and end, or Middle (a track starting at about 30:00, from 25:00 to 35:00). A clock may set its own rule for the playlist.
A track can be in several playlists at once. Removing it from one playlist does not remove it from the library.
Rules set on a playlist apply to each of its tracks separately, together with the track's own rules. A play rule limits how often a track may repeat; the placement rule decides where and how many.

usage: Filter the list by type; the "In clocks" column shows each placement rule. Open a playlist to rename it, change its type and placement rule, add or remove tracks, and set its play rules. Use the play button next to a track to listen to it.
steps: Click Add playlist, enter a name, and choose a type.
Choose the placement in clocks, for example Fill for music or Spread 2 for jingles.
Add tracks with the track picker. Search by title or artist and tick the tracks you want.
Add play rules that every track of the playlist must follow, for example "Music rotation".
Add the playlist to a clock on the Clocks page.
mistakes: Trying to put tracks in order. The order is not stored; placement rules and inserts shape the hour.
Making a playlist so small that its play rules block every track. With a track interval of 72 hours, a fill playlist needs many tracks.
Giving a music playlist a rule other than Fill and then using it alone in a clock. A clock needs at least one fill playlist.
Deleting a playlist that clocks still use. Remove it from the clocks first.

example.title: Music and jingles for the daytime clock
example.text: Create "Pop hits" of type music with the rule Fill and add 300 songs; attach the play rule "Music rotation". Create "Jingles" with the rule Spread 2. A clock with both plays an hour of pop songs with two jingles apart from each other, and no song repeats within three days.

operations.create: The type is required. The placement rule is Fill unless you choose another one.
operations.edit: Track changes apply to hours that are planned from now on. A changed placement rule rebuilds the planned hours of the clocks that use the playlist; the page shows that rebuild.
operations.delete: A playlist used by a clock, as a playlist or as the source of an insert, cannot be deleted. The message lists the clocks that use it.

name.label: Name
name.text: A name you will recognize in clocks, for example "Pop hits".

type_id.label: Playlist type
type_id.text: A label for filters and badges. One clock may combine playlists of different types.

clock_rule.label: Placement in clocks
clock_rule.text: Fill, Spread, Start, End, Start and end, or Middle. A clock may override it for itself.

clock_count.label: Tracks per hour
clock_count.text: For Spread only: how many tracks of the playlist play in the hour, 1 to 12.

track_ids.label: Tracks
track_ids.text: The tracks of the pool. Their order is not stored.

rule_ids.label: Play rules
rule_ids.text: Rules that apply to every track of this playlist, checked for each track separately.
